name: Action! "Television" Championship
epitaph: Action!'s Action! "Television" Championship's first recorded champion is Keith Scott Zimmerman. The fed's own record carries 5 reigns on it, across 4 different champions. The longest is Keith Scott Zimmerman's, 21 days from 2003-01-06. Sweet Aroma held it at the end of the surviving record.
notes: The '(t)' marker on the Pressure Point 59 match Dirk $eller vs. Sweet Aroma (5 May 2003) is the fed's own champion tag for it, exactly as (A!)/(b)/(c)/(D) mark its four filed belts -- treated here as a real lineage the record carries, served as an unfiled belt with its lineage. Keith Scott Zimmerman is billed as already champion ('the newest member of the Action family... also the "Television Champion" of Action!') at his in-fiction DEBUT on the first of the nine matches -- the title is presented as pre-existing his arrival, self-proclaimed/'unsanctioned' (his own word, in the Pressure Point 44 match of 6 January 2003), never sanctioned by the fed's own record. Grade for the whole chain: primary-source (every reign is read from the matches' own texts, at the grade the text supports; two turnovers are undated on-page and bracketed, see action-tv-002/003's conflict fields).

name: Action Championship
epitaph: Action!'s Action Championship was first won by Chris Fear on 20 March 2002. The fed's own record carries 9 reigns on it, across 8 different champions. The longest is Jeff Garvin's, 143 days from 31 August 2003. One of its reigns ended outside a match — stripped from the holder; another changed hands off-page, by the fed's own owner's award rather than a match. Phil Atken held it at the end of the surviving record, his own status left open twice on the fed's own last show.
notes: Pre-history residue, 2002-03-31 ('Resentment' special): see action-001's note -- an overturned title-change finish, not a reign, with no title-log row. Two mechanical conflicts on this belt are resolved by legacy log rows 2538/2539 (action-007/action-008); see their notes. Jeff Garvin's second reign ends off-page: Reed Young hands the belt to Phil Atken on Pressure Point 90 (2004-01-21), no strip shown; Atken's own reign is filed open to the fed's own record's end (Pressure Point 92, 2004-04-07, leaves his status 'unclear' twice, and the fed's own last word follows 9 July 2004) rather than given an invented loss.

name: Bantam Championship
epitaph: Action!'s Bantam Championship was first won by Joey Malone on 10 July 2002. The fed's own record carries 8 reigns on it, across 8 different champions. The longest is Joey Malone's, 81 days from 10 July 2002. Keith Scott Zimmerman held it at the end of the surviving record.
notes: Pre-history residue, 2002-03-31 ('Resentment' special): a ladder match for a Bantam Championship the fed's OWN OWNER character retracts on air minutes later ('it's way too soon to bring out the B Title'), before the belt's real creation by tournament on 2002-07-10 (bantam-001). No reign, no championship existed to change hands; see bantam-001's note. Two mechanical conflicts on this belt are resolved by the legacy log row 2546 (bantam-007); see its note.

name: Carnage Championship
epitaph: Action!'s Carnage Championship was first won by Simon Seaman on 26 May 2002. The fed's own record carries 6 reigns on it, across 5 different champions. The longest is Max Danger's, 195 days from 17 March 2003. HardCase held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Dyad Championship
epitaph: Action!'s Dyad Championship was first won by Clit 'n Candy on 25 August 2002. The fed's own record carries 7 reigns on it, across 7 different champions. The longest is Arcade & Son's, 126 days from 25 May 2003. The International Workrate Connection held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: King of Submission
epitaph: A submission tournament whose final was fought at Blood, Sweat, and Tears in February 2003 for a three-foot trophy. Max Danger won it when Jeff Garvin's corner threw in the towel, and the trophy stood at his table at the fed's own awards night a month later.
